property.name: start
property.description-key: Start of the gantt chart boundary, as a date such as 2026-01-01. Leave blank to use the earliest task date.

property.name: end
property.description-key: End of the gantt chart boundary, as a date such as 2026-12-31. Leave blank to use the latest task date.

property.name: fields
property.description-key: Which columns the chart reads, as JSON: {"task":"title","start":"startDate","end":"endDate","progress":"progress","parent":"parentId","group":"crew","row":{"id":"employee.id","label":"employee.name"},"category":"","color":"","locked":""}. Every entry is optional and takes a column name or lookup.column. Task, group and row also take an id and a label. In a canvas app, write it with JSON({...}).

property.name: options
property.description-key: How the chart looks and what a user may do, as JSON: {"density":"comfortable","timeScale":"day","colorBy":"status","legend":"Day shift=#0F6CBD; *=#8A8886","showToolbar":true,"showCurrentTime":true,"showProgress":true,"showLegend":true,"groupRows":true,"allowMove":false,"allowResize":false,"showSettings":false}. Every entry is optional; the values shown are the defaults. Turn showSettings on while building the app for a settings panel that previews changes and writes both properties out to copy, then turn it off again. In a canvas app, write it with JSON({...}).

property.name: selectedTaskId
property.description-key: The taskId of the bar the user selected. Empty while a row is selected.

property.name: selectedRowId
property.description-key: The row the user selected: the group value for a group heading, the row id for a grouped row, otherwise the taskId of the row. Empty while a bar is selected.

property.name: lastEdit
property.description-key: The last move or resize, as JSON: {"stamp":1,"action":"move","taskId":"T-1","title":"Mobilisation","start":"2026-09-20T09:00:00+08:00","end":"2026-09-27T17:00:00+08:00"}. Read it in OnChange with ParseJSON and switch on action. Stamp counts the edits, so repeating one — dragging a bar back where it was — still reaches OnChange. Blank until the first edit.

property.name: draftFields
property.description-key: The field mapping last applied from the settings panel, as JSON. Blank until Apply is used. Store it in OnChange, for example to a settings table, and read Field mapping from there so the setting is kept.

property.name: draftOptions
property.description-key: The options last applied from the settings panel, as JSON. Blank until Apply is used. Store it alongside Applied field mapping and read Options from there.
